messages:
Leah: Quick sync — we need to lock what goes into the next 2-week iteration post-launch. We have 3 customer escalations, a latency regression spike (~+18% p95), and a backlog of enhancement asks. Proposing a simple decision rule: regressions P0/P1 (customer impact or >5% metric delta) => immediate slot; everything else => enhancement lane and groom for following wave. Thoughts?

Sam: +1 for clear cutoff. Can we define how to measure the 5%? rolling 7d vs baseline?

Leah: Good call. Use rolling 7d vs last 30d baseline (same as monitoring dashboards). I'll add the metric link: https://app.redwood/metrics/launch/latency (internal)

Jin: Agree with rule. One add: if fix is <2 dev-days and blocks onboarding flows, we can fast-track even if metric delta <5%.

Olga: From QA — we have a flaky e2e tied to the playback flow that's tripping customer tickets. Hard to reproduce locally, but reproduction rate ~40% in canary trace. I'd mark that high.

Maya: Customer success here — two paying customers opened P1 tickets complaining about intermittent 502s during streaming responses. They're asking for a timeline. They'd be >likely to churn if unresolved in 3 weeks.

Carlos: Support data: ~18 tickets total this week referencing streaming failures; trend started after the launch patch. I can drop a CSV in the doc.

Leah: Ok, consensus seems to prioritize the streaming/502 problem. Sam/Jin can we estimate?

Sam: I'll take the lead on triage. First pass: reproduce in staging with a recorded trace and validate if it's a networking/timeout or kv-cache eviction issue. Est ETA for triage: EOD tomorrow. If it's a simple timeout constant we can patch in <1d.

Jin: Assigning Sam + Olga for triage. If triage shows infra or runtime-level bug, we escalate to eng-runtime. @Sam please @mention infra if needed.

Sam: Got it. I'll open an internal ticket and link to the customer tickets. JQL I'm using for backlog filter:
```
project = REDWOOD AND labels in (postlaunch, streaming) AND (type = Bug OR priority >= P1) ORDER BY created DESC
```

Priya: To preserve UX momentum, can we scope one small enhancement into the sprint that improves the streaming UX (progress indicator)? It's low-risk and increases perceived reliability even if the backend fix takes longer.

Leah: Good idea. But we need to be strict: only one enhancement slot this sprint unless regression fixes free up bandwidth. Which enhancement has highest ROI?

Priya: The progress indicator + retry CTA has the best CS signal. Design: 6-8 hours, dev ~1.5 days.

Maya: CS supports that — it reduces churn risk and gives us something to offer affected customers as a partial improvement.

Jin: OK: plan for sprint: 2 regression slots (streaming 502 + flaky playback e2e), 1 enhancement (progress indicator), leftover small bugs into grooming. If streaming triage finishes fast we can backfill with the next highest enhancement from the list (see doc: https://redwood.in/ops/iteration-playbook).

Leah: Acceptance criteria for each slot (proposed):
- Streaming 502: reproduce case, root cause identified, mitigation or patch in canary, rollback plan and customer comms draft.
- Playback e2e: flakiness <5% on canary + fix in staging.
- Progress indicator: UX signed off by Priya, unit tests + e2e happy path.

Olga: I'll add test cases and a flaky test suppression list for the playback flow so we don't get noisy alerts during triage.

Sam: Opening ticket now: REDWOOD-5021, linking 18 support tickets, ETA triage complete 1709540400 (tomorrow 18:00 UTC).

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for service stream-handler v1.3.8-canary at 1709460000

Carlos: Dropping the support CSV in the doc: https://redwood.docs/supcases/streaming_feb.csv — highlights attached.

Leah: Thanks all. Action items: Sam/Olga triage + REDWOOD-5021, Jin to coordinate eng-runtime if escalated, Priya to queue progress indicator design, Maya/Carlos to prep customer comms template. We’ll review status in Thurs triage (standup thread). If anything blocks, ping this thread. :thumbsup:
